message: No detected input validation: No schema checks, dtype assertions, or value-range guards are applied to any user-supplied inputs (dropdown values, text fields, user IDs) before they are passed to recommender or other ML methods.

No detected untrusted source handling: No checksums, signed URLs, pinned revisions, or authentication mechanisms are visible for any remote data sources (e.g., Google Trends API used in Lab 3 or any dataset loading).
No detected label flipping detection: The code contains no checks for label distribution anomalies, validation of label values against an expected set, or any label-noise detection tooling.

No detected data poisoning defenses: The code performs no outlier detection, statistical anomaly checks, or filtering of suspicious training samples; it simply loads and passes data to model objects without any poisoning defenses.

No detected model integrity verification: Models are loaded via Recommender(), SpamIdentifier(), SentimentInferencing(), and KeywordOverTimeTrends() constructors with no hash checks, signature verification, or pinned revision evident in the code.
No detected label distribution validation: The code contains no label distribution checks, class balance validation, or anomalous sample detection before or during training.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no trigger detection, activation analysis, or gradient anomaly detection of any kind present in the code.
No detected differential privacy: No differential privacy libraries (Opacus, TensorFlow Privacy, DP-SGD, etc.) or mechanisms are used anywhere in the code.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: No adversarial robustness testing frameworks or attack simulations (Foolbox, ART, FGSM, PGD, etc.) are present anywhere in the code.

No detected metric tampering protection: The code is a Dash web application with no evaluation metrics computation, no held-out test set isolation, no signed/hashed evaluation data, and no multiple independent metrics used.
No detected input sanitization: User inputs from dropdowns and text fields are passed directly to recommender, spam, and sentiment model functions without any shape, range, or schema validation.
No detected output bounds checks: Model outputs such as recommendation lists and classifications are returned directly to the UI with no NaN guards, probability bounds checks, or sanity validation.

No detected prompt injection defenses: Although Lab 2 uses text-in classification models, there is no input filtering, output content moderation, or jailbreak/injection detection applied to any text inputs.
